identification: Pair of Tasmanian spindle-back 'utility/railway' chairs consistent with the George Peddle (Hobart, active c1884-1920s) Nabowla/utility pattern: curved flat crest rail, five bead-and-cove turned spindles (outer ones as back posts) with ring turnings, deeply dished saddle seat with shaped (scalloped) front edge, ring-turned splayed legs, double side stretchers and front stretcher. Timber looks like blackwood (honey colour, seat shows figure), old worn finish, top rails worn. No jawbone supports. No stamp visible in the 2 photos. Armitage estimate A$800-1,000 for the pair.

viewing_check: Confirm the timber is blackwood (not elm/beech): look under the seat and at the end grain. Look under the seats and on the back legs for any stamp or pencil mark. Check the turnings match Peddle's bead-and-cove style, that joints are tight, and for seat cracks or replaced legs. If it does not look convincingly Tasmanian blackwood, treat as ordinary kitchen chairs (A$100-250 the pair).
